payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Add priority and backorders
root.objective: Add order priority and backorders across the warehouse stack without regressing existing behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Orders placed without an explicit priority continue to behave as standard orders.
Invalid supplied priorities are rejected by the domain layer.
Reservations record backorders instead of aborting on short stock and keep the order cancellable.
Backorders flow into service events, analytics, API state, and presentation.
Express orders are prioritized within each fulfillment wave.
The new g6 probe is deterministic and scriptable.

repositoryEvidence.observation: The domain order model currently has id, lines, and status, and reserveOrder throws on insufficient stock rather than recording shortages.
Existing order tests provide the natural regression harness for reservation, transition, and new priority/backorder cases.
WarehouseService currently exposes createOrder, reserve, transition, snapshot, and a shared event stream with order.created, order.reserved, and order.status_changed events.
Existing service tests cover the orchestration layer that will need to assert backorder emission and new exposure paths.
planFulfillment currently keeps the input order of assigned orders within each wave and does not inspect order priority.
Planner tests already exist and can lock in wave ordering behavior after introducing priority sorting.
History analytics currently derives counts, creations, reservations, and alerts from events, but no backorders count.
Journal tests provide the regression surface for new derived analytics fields.
The HTTP server already exposes state, fulfillment, history, events, orders, and simulation routes and serializes the current warehouse snapshot.
Server tests are available to lock in the current response shapes and new backorder exposure.
The tower renderer currently visualizes inventory quantities only and does not distinguish order priority.
Presentation tests can verify the new express-versus-standard rendering behavior.
The existing probe shape exports main() as a JSON string builder and writes exactly one JSON object plus newline when executed directly.
Probe tests show how deterministic output and direct-invocation behavior are currently verified.
Scripts currently include build, test, typecheck, study:probe, study:wc1-probe, study:wc2-probe, study:wc3-probe, and start, but no study:g6-probe.
